headline: Council welcomes Fukuyama City Assembly members, discusses Lahaina recovery

meeting.summary: Council members discussed West Maui water, where the county controls delivery of 23 percent, and a county insurance gap program for homeowners rebuilding. The delegation was set to give an evening presentation at UH Maui College.
meeting.recap: The Maui County Council held a special meeting to welcome visiting members of the Fukuyama City Assembly.[[0:01:59]] A 2008 Council resolution made Maui County and Fukuyama City sister cities.[[0:02:12]] Power is shut off when wind tops 45 miles per hour and humidity is under 45 percent, a council member said.[[0:19:28]] The county controls delivery of 23 percent of West Maui water, with 77 percent handled by private companies.[[0:21:33]] The county's reclaimed water, which is treated wastewater, fell from 5 million to about 3 million gallons a day after the fire.[[0:23:05]] A council member said federal money is helping rebuild, but the paperwork makes it hard for families to get it.[[0:25:59]] The Army Corps of Engineers cleaned up the town, using cultural monitors.[[0:28:27]] The county started an insurance gap program to help homeowners rebuild; gaps are often $300,000 to $500,000.[[0:34:41]] The program uses deed restrictions, limits written into the property deed, so homes are not quickly resold for profit.[[0:35:29]] Everyone was invited to a group photo before the delegation's evening presentation at UH Maui College.[[0:46:29]]
meeting.next: The delegation was set to give an evening presentation at UH Maui College.
